Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
ABC: House Republicans propose stricter voting requirements as Trump administration eyes the midterms [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013026_3&amount=25]
Folks, we've been warning you about the SAVE Act since it was introduced, since it's a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote.
Well, there's a new champion in the " anti-voting legislation " category with the introduction of the Make Elections Great Again (MEGA) Act. The new bill goes far beyond even the SAVE Act, with the MEGA Act now being called " the most extreme voting restrictions ever proposed at the federal level ."
The name also tells you everything you need to know about the target audience for this bill. With Trump focused on re-litigating the 2020 election, t his legislation would give him all the power he would need to take federal control of the upcoming midterms .
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013026_3&amount=35]
While the SAVE Act focused almost exclusively on requiring voters to produce documentary proof of citizenship when registering, the MEGA Act is far more sweeping. It would:
* Impose a strict photo ID requirement to vote
* Create a centralized voter surveillance system in every state
* Mandate constant voter roll purges, gutting the “Motor Voter” law that expanded access to voter registration
* Bar states from counting ballots that arrive after Election Day
* Ban universal mail voting, in which states mail a ballot to all registered voters
* Bar the federal funding for voter registration by outside groups
* Unleash lawsuits against election officials
Estimates said the SAVE Act could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities. The MEGA Act would be much, much worse.
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the MEGA Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013026_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=013026_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=013026_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=013026_3&amount=50]

The scariest parts of the MEGA Act are how it goes after so much more than proof-of-citizenship at registration. States aren't mandated to provide ID to eligible citizens, but the MEGA Act would require citizens to show the right kind of ID every time they went to vote. This creates inequality, like in Texas, where you can vote with a hunting license ( which doesn't require proof of citizenship ) but you can't vote with a college photo ID.
This bill targets voter registration as well, demanding that eligible voters re-prove their citizenship every election, while also requiring states to " take affirmative steps... on an ongoing basis " every 30 days to check and verify their voter rolls. How would they check them? Using a nationwide federal database controlled by MAGA partisans, of course . And the bill calls for all these measures to be in place before we vote in November's general election.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights said about the SAVE Act. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
His words ring even more true about the MEGA Act. This bill is nothing less than an all-out partisan assault on our fundamental right to vote . If made law, this bill would codify MAGA's power for decades to come, invalidating millions of eligible voters and ending our democracy for a generation or longer.
None of us can afford to sit on the sidelines, Team, and watch our fundamental right to vote die. Fight back against these cynical vote suppressors with $35 or whatever you can before it's too late >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013026_3&amount=35]

_POLITICO_ sent out a breaking news alert, calling my address "defiant." They're right. Because when federal immigration raids sweep through our communities as part of an ongoing attack on democracy nationwide, someone needs to stand up and fight back.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124393911/598457566/152256275?refcode=WUEFHM67_20260130_MillsSplit_ALL_v1s1&sourceid=1057657&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZjYwMzU4ZC0yN2ZlLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=s8zzw-45Q7XKxYBJHzzMV4PntOh5peu_tFiPrs7P42Q=)
But my fight for Maine didn't start with ICE. **For years, I've stood up to special interests, corporate greed, and anyone who tried to push Maine people around. **

I’ve stood up for reproductive rights. Secured free community college. Provided free meals for public school students across the state. Signed Paid Family Leave into law. Expanded Medicaid on my first day as governor, providing health care to over 100,000 people.

Those things and more go into the message I delivered on behalf of every single person in our state – one that needed to be heard loud and clear:
_"I say to the people of Maine: We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. And to anyone outside these halls, including any federal officials, I say: if you seek to harm Maine people, you will have to go through me first."_
Maine deserves a senator with a backbone. One who is a battle-tested fighter who won't back down when times get tough. Not someone who falls in line with Donald Trump and puts party over people.

**The truth is, Democrats can't win the Senate without winning Maine.** And right now, a recent poll shows me neck and neck with Susan Collins – 43% to 43%. I can't win without grassroots supporters like you standing with me.

clean_body: | = Peter, it's Janet. Earlier this week, I delivered my last State of the State address as governor. Missed it? I've recapped it for you below, but first – = | = POLITICO sent out a breaking news alert, calling my address "defiant." They're right. Because when federal immigration raids sweep through our communities as part of an ongoing attack on democracy nationwide, someone needs to stand up and fight back. = But my fight for Maine didn't start with ICE. For years, I've stood up to special interests, corporate greed, and anyone who tried to push Maine people around. I’ve stood up for reproductive rights. Secured free community college. Provided free meals for public school students across the state. Signed Paid Family Leave into law. Expanded Medicaid on my first day as governor, providing health care to over 100,000 people. Those things and more go into the message I delivered on behalf of every single person in our state – one that needed to be heard loud and clear: "I say to the people of Maine: We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. And to anyone outside these halls, including any federal officials, I say: if you seek to harm Maine people, you will have to go through me first." Maine deserves a senator with a backbone. One who is a battle-tested fighter who won't back down when times get tough. Not someone who falls in line with Donald Trump and puts party over people. The truth is, Democrats can't win the Senate without winning Maine. And right now, a recent poll shows me neck and neck with Susan Collins – 43% to 43%. Right now, the daily deluge of breaking news may feel overwhelming or bleak to a lot of us. It may feel nearly impossible to bridge the divide that has come to characterize our modern politics. But that’s exactly what extremists want – they want normal people to point their finger at each other instead of coming together to solve problems.

We can’t give in to that. I firmly believe that we as Americans have more in common than what separates us, and I believe that we can make meaningful progress without sacrificing our values or resorting to mudslinging.

Here in Southwest Washington, we help our neighbors and we don’t back down when things get tough. While that approach has set our grassroots campaign apart from the rest, it has also put me squarely in the sights of far-right extremists whose only goal is to expand their power by further sowing division and chaos.

name: David Hogg
subject: Keep going, Peter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
I know how this moment feels.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260130-1&t=1&akid=3099%2E587540%2ESJxln2)
Peter,
I know how this moment feels.
Everyday, we’re waking up to fresh chaos and louder headlines. The stakes are high, and even the people who care the most are exhausted. If you’re feeling that burnout right now, you’re not alone — and you’re not wrong for feeling that way.
I experienced an extreme form of it after the midterm elections in 2018, following the shooting in Parkland. After the shooting, thousands of people (older adults in particular) said the same thing to the student activists from Parkland over and over: “You know my generation really screwed things up. Thank God you kids are here to save us.” Many of us, including myself, took that to heart. I remember completely losing track of what day it was, working so hard to turn out and rally young people to vote to defeat the NRA. In those days, the only way I would let myself stop was if I was so ill I physically could not get out of bed. Then, in November, Democrats won back the House — _but basically nothing changed._ It was devastating. So the next year I traveled the country speaking with activists and community leaders who have been combatting gun violence for decades. From those conversations, and a lot of therapy, I learned the one thing that has enabled me to keep going 8 years later.
I realized how many people had been working to prevent gun violence for decades long before I was even born. From that I realized I can take breaks because when I am not working there are other people out there doing the work and when they need a break they can rest knowing myself and others are stepping up when they can’t. That’s why when the time came for me to go to college and step back from day-to-day activism, I knew I could. I knew I could step back when I saw people like my friend and gun violence prevention advocate, Maxwell Frost, step up, run for Congress, get elected, and play a major role in the creation of the Office of Gun Violence Prevention at the White House.
And guess what...
In the two years of that office’s existence — prior to Trump totally dismantling it — we saw the two largest one-year drops in gun homicides in our nation's history. That's the power of bringing young people into government who understand the experience of a school shooter drill.
**That’s why Leaders We Deserve exists. We aren’t here to elect younger versions of those in power now, but to instead bring into power truly generational leaders who get results, like Maxwell Frost.**
So if you are exhausted now, it’s better to rest before you burn out. And you can rest knowing that there is a generation of new leaders we are supporting coming into power who can pick up the torch and get it to the finish line. But only with your support.
**[If you’re able, will you pitch in $5 now to help us hit our $25,000 end-of-month goal and elect the next generation of fighters today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260130_1_eom.SEl87J&refcode=em20260130-3099&amount=5&t=2&akid=3099%2E587540%2ESJxln2)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260130_1_eom.SEl87J&amount=5&refcode=em20260130-3099&t=21&akid=3099%2E587540%2ESJxln2)**
Thank you for staying in this fight even when it's hard.
— David

Hi Peter,
The Trump administration’s assault on Minnesota isn’t a matter of immigration enforcement. It is a campaign of organized brutality against the people of our state.
It’s chaos. It’s illegal. And it’s un-American.
In recent weeks, masked agents have abducted children, racially profiled off-duty police officers, and broken into the homes of elderly citizens without warrants to drag them outside in freezing temperatures.
The people responsible have yet to be held accountable. Instead, Donald Trump’s DOJ is picking legal battles with me in an attempt to intimidate me into silence.
Well guess what? It won’t work. Minnesotans aren’t abandoning their values — and neither will I.
I’m going to keep defending the rule of law and pushing back against this abuse of power so we can get back to what matters most to our state: allowing freedom, opportunity, and security for everyone.
But here’s the deal: fights like this aren’t cheap. **That’s why I need your help.**

Fellow American,

Democrats are outspending Republicans by historic margins across the country, in races that wouldn't have been considered battleground races just a few years ago. They're relying on a radical base of megadonors and extremist special interest groups to fuel their campaigns.

We don't have their base of extremist megadonors. We're a grassroots-powered campaign. That means, to compete, every ad and voter outreach campaign needs to be carefully planned, budgeted for, and executed. That's where our End-of-Month fundraising deadlines come into play - _especially the first of the Election Year._

clean_body: Democrats are outspending Republicans by historic margins across the country, in races that wouldn’t have been considered battleground races just a few years ago. | Fellow American, I know this is the time you start receiving a lot of emails about the first End-of-Month fundraising deadline of 2026. Most of the emails will tell you it's an important deadline, but they will rarely explain why these End-of-Month deadlines are so critical to a campaign's success. That's why I wanted to take a minute to break down why our Saturday deadline is so important and not just a marketing gimmick. After you hear my explanation, I hope you'll join our fight by pitching in a few dollars ahead of January 31st. Democrats are outspending Republicans by historic margins across the country, in races that wouldn't have been considered battleground races just a few years ago. They're relying on a radical base of megadonors and extremist special interest groups to fuel their campaigns. We don't have their base of extremist megadonors. We're a grassroots-powered campaign. That means, to compete, every ad and voter outreach campaign needs to be carefully planned, budgeted for, and executed. That's where our End-of-Month fundraising deadlines come into play - especially the first of the Election Year. Months in advance, my campaign team sets specific monthly fundraising benchmarks to run the ads and target the voters we need to secure victory. These fundraising targets allow my team to plan our winning voter outreach strategy and combat anything the Democrats throw at us. In a race this expensive and contentious, One down month or a missed deadline could permanently put us on the defensive, jeopardizing our Republican majority. With less than 48 hours left before January ends, my team is only $2,030 short of our benchmark. I know it doesn't sound like a lot, but with the amount Democrats are spending against us, EVERY dollar matters. Even coming up a few dollars short means critical campaign operations will have to be scaled back. will give my team the resources they need to execute a winning campaign strategy to keep this seat in Republican hands. Thanks for standing with me, Steve Daines P.S. To give an idea of what we're up against. Democrats spent over $90 million in Montana in the 2024 election. The biggest reason we came out on top was because of the support of grassroots conservatives like you. Steve Daines is a fifth-generation Montanan, life-long sportsman and father of four serving the people of Montana as their Senator. Steve is committed to always putting Montana first as he works to bring real change to Washington and fights for more jobs, less government and common sense solutions to get our country back on track. Senator Steve Daines | | Paid for by Steve Daines for Montana

Friend, I want to start with something simple – and important: **You’re not an ATM to me.** Too many campaigns treat people like a transaction or a target. That’s not how I believe this work should be done, and it’s not how we’ve run this campaign from day one. If you’ve read a few of my emails before, I hope you’ve noticed the difference. We don’t rely on panic or scare tactics to get attention. We’re upfront about the stakes, honest about the work ahead, and respectful of people like you, who make this campaign possible. Because this campaign isn’t powered by fear and ALL CAPS messages that make you never want to donate to a campaign again – it’s powered by people who have hope for the future we’re building together, chipping in what they can, when they can. That grassroots support made it possible to win a Trump-won district and keep showing up for mid-Michigan – pushing for affordable health care, lower costs, and policies that actually improve people’s day-to-day lives. And it’s what’s going to help us protect this seat and win again in November. # **Trump brokers deal to push forward massive funding package**
Senate Republicans and Democrats reached an agreement to move forward with a massive government funding package **[after President Trump intervened to broker a deal](https://substack.com/redirect/0e6d57c1-a0da-4bf8-a97a-3b0a7bf1bc68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. The agreement strips out the controversial Department of Homeland Security funding bill and replaces it with a two-week funding extension for the agency.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e6d57c1-a0da-4bf8-a97a-3b0a7bf1bc68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Government Shutdown Inevitable** \- Despite the Senate progress, a partial government shutdown is all but guaranteed because the funding deadline is midnight Friday and the House is not in session until next week at the earliest. The modified five-bill package and DHS continuing resolution must be agreed to by the House, where resistance is mounting among fiscal hawks.
**Both Sides Make Compromises** \- Republicans had to accept dropping the DHS bill despite pushing the original six-bill package, while Democrats made concessions after arguing that any continuing resolution would give Trump a "slush fund" for immigration operations, and renegotiating the Homeland funding bill could backfire since Democrats originally agreed to the current restrictions.

# **Epstein claimed Gates sought STD treatment after "sex with Russian girls"**
Jeffrey Epstein alleged in a 2013 draft statement **[that Bill Gates asked an adviser to provide medicine for sexually transmitted diseases](https://substack.com/redirect/234a207e-9123-4552-aa00-14d760a536f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** contracted from "sex with Russian girls" -- claims a Gates spokesperson called "completely false."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/234a207e-9123-4552-aa00-14d760a536f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Why it matters:** The allegations appear in 3.5 million pages of documents released by the Justice Department on Friday, revealing Epstein's apparent attempts to leverage damaging information about powerful figures.
**What 's in the documents:** Epstein, writing in the voice of Gates' science adviser Boris Nikolic, claimed he was asked to help Gates obtain drugs, facilitate "illicit trysts," and secretly slip antibiotics to then-wife Melinda French Gates. The draft also referenced threatening to expose Gates' alleged 2017 affair with Russian bridge player Mila Antonova.
**The big picture:** Gates has repeatedly insisted his relationship with Epstein was solely focused on philanthropy, though he acknowledged in 2021 it was a "huge mistake to spend time with him." The newly released files include photos of Gates with Epstein, taken years after Epstein registered as a sex offender in 2008.

Legendary actress Catherine O'Hara, beloved for her Emmy-winning role as Moira Rose on _Schitt 's Creek_ **[and as the frantic mom in](https://substack.com/redirect/d5bd0b9d-d2bf-4ed5-92cc-c81fbabe2a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** _**[Home Alone](https://substack.com/redirect/06104772-b330-45cc-b353-bf8bb105a342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_**[,](https://substack.com/redirect/06104772-b330-45cc-b353-bf8bb105a342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/06104772-b330-45cc-b353-bf8bb105a342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)has died at 71. She passed away Friday at her Los Angeles home following a brief illness, her agency CAA confirmed, shocking fans and drawing tributes from co-stars including Macaulay Culkin and Pedro Pascal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d5bd0b9d-d2bf-4ed5-92cc-c81fbabe2a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tributes Pour In** : Macaulay Culkin shared an emotional Instagram post lamenting lost time with his on-screen mom, while Pedro Pascal called her a "genius" who brought eternal light; Justin Theroux and Ron Howard also mourned her immense talent and warmth.
* **Recent Frailty Noted** : O'Hara appeared frail at her last public event, the Emmys in September, and missed the 2026 Golden Globes despite a Best Supporting Actress nomination for _The Studio_ ; she received a career honor at TIFF months earlier.
* **Illness Led to Hospital** : Los Angeles Fire Department responded to her home at 4:48 a.m. for medical aid, transporting the approximately 70-year-old woman in serious condition; she died later that day, survived by husband Bo Welch and sons Matthew and Luke.

* * *
# Climate radicals storm synagogue to harass Democratic Rep over budget vote
Climate Defiance activists **[stormed a New York synagogue event](https://substack.com/redirect/06104772-b330-45cc-b353-bf8bb105a342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** this week, ambushing Democratic Rep. Tom Suozzi with diapers and kneepads to mock his vote funding ICE by $10 billion, prompting the congressman to later express regret for defying party lines on the Homeland Security bill.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06104772-b330-45cc-b353-bf8bb105a342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Activists ambush Suozzi** with crude props including adult diapers and kneepads, accusing him of cowardice and collaboration with "fascists" during a temple appearance.
* **Protest targets ICE vote** where Suozzi joined six other Democrats in a narrow 210-207 House passage to boost funding for ICE and Border Patrol operations.
* **A Jewish protester condemned** the congressman's support, sarcastically thanking him for making streets feel like "masked Gestapo" while seizing a microphone at the synagogue.

I spent decades as a sideline reporter for professional football and basketball. I covered more Minnesota games than I can count. And I raised two children with my husband outside Minneapolis. I love Minnesota. However, what's happening here hits a little too close to home. 1. I watched as Tim Walz sent my tax dollars to fraudulent daycares. 2. I watched as career politicians handed out billions to illegal immigrants while our veterans slept on the streets. 3. I watched as violent rioters burned down my city in 2020. 4. I watched as protesters stormed a St. Paul church to intimidate Sunday worshippers. We have the opportunity of a LIFETIME to take back this state in the name of sanity. I know we can win, but only if I can fund a winning campaign. Will you help me get off the ground by becoming a founding donor today? Listen - as a sideline reporter and as a mother, I've seen up close and personal what the far-Left has done to our country. I saw the players kneeling during our national anthem. I saw the ladies on The View insinuate that I was a racist for not supporting Joe Biden. I saw the activists calling for male swimmers to compete against our girls. I saw the radical ideologies cropping up in my kids' classrooms. This goes against everything I believe in. When I shock the world and win this race, this divisiveness and corruption will come to a SCREECHING HALT. Unfortunately, the far-Left has raised 100+ million dollars to destroy our momentum and end my campaign for good. That's exactly what will happen if this email fails. If you’re
wondering who really calls the shots at the Supreme Court right now, don’t
overthink it.

It’s Donald Trump.

When Trump’s agenda hits a wall in the lower courts, he doesn’t wait. He
sprints to the Supreme Court’s so-called emergency docket to get the
ruling he wants.

And like clockwork, the conservative majority delivers.

More than 75% of the time, the Court gives Trump exactly what he wants. No
full briefing. No real scrutiny. No transparency. Just rushed, back-room
orders that shove his policies forward while real people pay the price.

The emergency docket is supposed to be for emergencies only, not Trump’s
personal cheat code to circumvent the law.

Through the emergency docket — or “shadow docket” — the Court has greenlit
mass firings of federal workers, stripped humanitarian protections from
immigrants, and banned transgender people from military service.

The justices call these decisions “temporary...”
Tell that to the immigrants unjustly deported or to the workers who have
lost their jobs.

This is not business as usual.

We’re calling out the weaponization of the shadow docket. We’re exposing
how this Court bends the rules for Trump. We’re fighting to restore a
judiciary that works for the people — not one man. But taking on a
captured Court takes resources.

Wednesday, President Donald Trump took some time during a recent speech to compliment U.S. Senator Katie Britt.
The president was speaking at an all-day summit with administration officials, CEOs and philanthropists, where Sen. Britt was also in attendance.
During his speech, he promoted his new Trump Accounts program. Trump explained that under the new initiative, the federal government would deposit $1,000 for every child born between 2025 and 2028. He also took a moment to recognize several leaders in attendance, including Sen. Britt and her husband, Wesley.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt urges federal support for the I-10 Mobile River Bridge, Bayway Project in Alabama, emphasizing its significance as the largest shovel-ready infrastructure project in the country. Britt seeks assistance to overcome obstacles and move towards construction, with an estimated cost of $2.5 billion and recent $550 million federal funding awarded in 2024.

# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240658%2E444211%2ES0t9WW)
Tomorrow is the special election for Senate District 9, and it’s our first real chance this year to show what people-powered organizing can do in Texas.
This runoff isn’t just about one race. It’s about whether we start 2026 on offense with Democrats organizing everywhere, competing everywhere, and winning where pundits say we can’t.
Right now, Democrats have real opportunities to flip seats and build momentum across the state. But those wins don’t come from wishful thinking. They come from organizers on the ground, volunteers registering people, voters getting the information they need—and the resources to fuel that work. If we hesitate now, these opportunities pass us by.
Take SD9. Tomorrow, Democrat Taylor Rehmet heads into a competitive runoff in a district Donald Trump carried by more than 17 points last year. Taylor is a veteran, a union leader, and a lifelong member of this community. And last month, he finished first with 48% of the vote, beating out two Republicans.
**That’s what happens when organizing meets the moment.**
Districts that were written off across Texas are now within reach because voters are ready for leaders who actually reflect their values — and because grassroots teams are showing up and doing the hard work. That’s exactly what Powered by People is built for.
We’re running a statewide organizing program to turn close races into real wins — supporting candidates, mobilizing voters, registering Texans, and strengthening Democratic infrastructure everywhere. But to push through the finish line tomorrow and keep this momentum going, we need our grassroots community fully behind us.
